gen-gf-unkempt-gf-graduate: Graduate spreads its serif letters generously, with capitals and lowercase nearly the same height. Unkempt is the one with attitude, while Graduate does the quiet bookish work.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-archivo: Relaxed and loose, Walter Turncoat writes in tubular strokes that never vary in width. Archivo takes over with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height, a crisper sans-serif voice.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-asap: Walter Turncoat comes first, with curves as heavy as its stems, like cord. The pair's strongest quality is how that hand-drawn looseness sits against Asap's open arcs and near-capital-height lowercase.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-epilogue: Approachable from the first line, this pairing starts with Walter Turncoat's casual pen-and-paper letters. Epilogue then carries the text in curvy, wire-like monoline strokes with a tall lowercase, so a long page keeps moving without tiring.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-fira-sans: A tall middle band with shallow ascenders and descenders gives Walter Turncoat its look. Fira Sans, with s curves open wide at both ends, makes the strongest quality here a sturdy, large-x-height counterweight.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-public-sans: Walter Turncoat draws its uppercase from lines of one constant thickness, loose and handmade. Public Sans follows with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, so a long passage reads sturdy and trustworthy.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-supreme: Walter Turncoat keeps every stroke at one weight, giving it a bent-pipe, handwritten ease. Supreme brings a thick, heavy-looking band of sans-serif text, and next to the hand lettering it feels crisp and held open.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-manrope: Tubular strokes like bent copper pipe make Walter Turncoat instantly recognizable. Manrope sits beneath with bright gaps at every curve and a pen line of one width, so the page feels friendly rather than fussy.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-satoshi: Satoshi stands tall with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e that never looks squeezed. And Walter Turncoat above it adds a relaxed, hand-drawn looseness that makes that plain sans feel warmer.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-switzer: Relaxed and graceful, Walter Turncoat writes with casual pen-and-paper letters and a tall middle band. Switzer answers in wire-like, tubular forms with a tall waist line, so the handwriting and the Swiss tidiness trade places easily.
